limitations: Bounded randomized agreement with a saved solver is not proof of semantic completeness.
rule: Each uniquely coloured rectangular frame (non-0, non-5) encloses scattered grey (5) cells. Count the greys inside each frame's bounding box, sort frames by count ascending, and output one left-aligned bar per frame (its colour, length = count) on a 0 background whose width equals the largest count.
scope: Supports 2..5 frames with distinct colours from {1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9}, per-side border thickness 1..3, interiors 3..8 by 3..9, distinct grey counts 1..12, placed with at least one background cell between frames on a 12..30 canvas. Deliberately not supported: equal grey counts between frames (ambiguous sort), overlapping/touching frames, grey cells outside frames, non-zero backgrounds, repeated frame colours. Random scenes require colour 0 to strictly outnumber every other colour.
constraints: Frame colours are distinct and never 0 or 5
Grey counts are distinct across frames so the sort order is unambiguous
Frames are axis-aligned rectangles separated by at least one background cell, so each colour's bounding box equals its frame
All grey cells lie strictly inside a frame interior; none on borders or free background
At least two frames per scene, so the output is never a single trivial row
known_limitations: Grey counts are capped at 12 and interiors at 8x9, slightly smaller than the largest canonical frames
Frame placement uses rejection sampling, so small canvases usually yield only 2..3 frames
Previous draft's test fixture was reconstructed with height 20 and an off-by-one 2-frame; corrected here to the true 21x21 canvas with the 2-frame at rows 12..20 and greys at (15,5),(15,8),(17,7)
Colour 0 must be strictly most frequent: saved solver misidentifies background on dense thick-frame inputs. Counterexamples retained separately.
billing: Claude Max CLI; API credentials excluded; no API fallback
